So, there's a lot of glitch abuse in this run.

The most noticeable one being Accelerated Backwards Hopping or ABH. How it works is, in the source engine there's a speed cap. When you jump, you can go above the speed cap. To slow you down however, the game gives you momentum, either forwards or backwards of the way you're facing. How it determines that is if you're holding your backwards key (s) or not. If you aren't holding S, you gain backwards momentum (and hence the reason it's called Backwards Hopping), but you gain forwards momentum if you're holding S (known as Accelerated Forwards Hopping [AFH]). One of the variants of ABH is known as ASH or Accelerated Sideways Hopping. It uses the same principles of ABH, but instead you hold down A and S or D and S. This sends you forwards and to the right or left, so you have to adjust your camera accordingly. By holding a sideways key, it makes it so you don't lose momentum while in the air if you just held S.

Another one of the glitches is teleporting. Simply put, if you hit an NPC over the head with an object, they think they get stuck and teleport to where they're supposed to end up. Usually smaller objects work better, but it's possible to do it with larger objects.

Wall climbing: Wall climbing is a fairly simple glitch, in which you crouch on an object, then spam use and jump (bound to mouse wheel up and down). You end up jumping off the object, then grabbing it, pulling you up. Can't do this in the air however since any objects you grab get thrown in front of you.

Prop Clipping and save/load clipping: If you shove certain objects against a wall in a specific position, you force the object inside of your hitbox and gets you stuck. If you combine this with quick saveing and loading, the game tries to get you unstuck by pulling you downwards. So long as the object is inside of you and has collision (EG: You can stand on top of it), you can save/load clip downwards. Crouching and uncrouching does make a difference, gaining about 17 Hammer Units when crouched, but only ~0.75 while uncrouched.

Save deletion: Save deletion is a glitch where if you save and load on a map, then delete the most recent save, and try and reload that save, the game does a fail safe and loads the map as if you typed it in console. This includes giving you a set inventory, spawning NPC's, and in Water Hazard, spawning the air boat.

Damage Boosting: Damage boosting is taking damage on purpose to get height and/or speed. This is done with SMG grenades, regular grenades, and the rocket launcher. Mostly used for gaining a large amount of speed in a small amount of time/space.

Circle jumping: Falling under the same principle of ABH, if you hold A or S while sprinting and then turn your camera in tandem with the direction you're holding, you can gain a decent amount of speed (about 400 UPS).

Air strafing: Air control by turning the mouse and holding a directional key.

Grav punting: If you hit an object with the left click on the gravity gun while you're on top of it, you'll get a small boost. Unfortunately, this trick is random in the sense that if you do it in the same spot, you can get different heights.

Sharking: Holding jump (via space) in water to maintain momentum.

Quantum Crouching: If you crouch, then uncrouch, and during the uncrouch animation, hit and hold crouch, you'll do quantum crouching. What this does is displaces your hitbox and camera. This is only used once in Nova Prospekt (combined with a grav punt) to hit a button through a ceiling. It can however also be used to make enemies miss since they aim at your camera, and not at your hit box.

I believe that covers most of the glitches in Half-Life 2. If you're curious about other glitches, feel free to visit http://wiki.sourceruns.org/wiki/Category:Half-Life_2
